text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The armed forces will erect an Ataturk statue in the heart of an extremely religious Istanbul district, Sultanbeyli, before the November 10 anniversary of Ataturk's death.
- Parliament approves a new law on smoking, banning smoking in public places or where more than five people are present.
- Interior Minister Mehmet Agar is torn between whether to resign or stay in his post over a scandal about alleged links between the police and organised crime.
- President Suleyman Demirel says the alleged relationship between organised crime, police and government should be closely investigated.
- Necessary steps to shed light on alleged links between the police, organised crime and politicians cannot be taken.
- Police in the resort of Marmaris arrest suspects, linked with an illegal leftist organisation, in connection with the assassination of the brother of Turkish tycoon Sakip Sabanci.
- Setbacks remain in implementing the build-operate-transfer model.
- Two leftist MPs alleged that a special team and state-paid village guards burned villages on September 11 in the eastern provinces of Erzurum and Erzincan provinces.
- A Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) militant who refused to be a suicide bomber is executed by the group in the southern province of Adana.
